Increase the carved court size so the void becomes occupiable and not merely a narrow slot.
Open the court toward the access side indicated in program context so the ground threshold becomes legible.
Preserve a grounded connecting bar so the courtyard is anchored as one coherent neighborhood mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing macro into a courtyard-producing mass so the dominant gesture keeps its clean anchor while creating a usable public void tied to the neighborhood-living brief.
Carve a larger, more legible void rather than a thin seam; this should create a public court instead of a decorative split.
Align the new court opening to the program-frame access side so the frontage becomes a legible public threshold.
Keep a grounded lower connector so the split masses still read as one programmatic figure with active base continuity.
Moderate the split-wing section so the upper mass remains calm and the void reads as inhabitable rather than accidental.

rationale: The candidate reads as two chunky bar-like solids with a narrow slot between them. In plan and isometric the split is legible, so there is some hierarchy and repair integrity, but the form is not yet a convincing neighborhood-living mass. The main failure is that the ground response to the access edge is weak: the blue frontage is met by a sealed edge rather than a public threshold, court, or undercut. The central void is too thin and semantically inactive to count as usable public space. The silhouette is also not meaningfully sectioned; it looks like a generic split block rather than a program-bearing ground-plus-upper hierarchy. Because the form is only partially coherent and lacks a legible active edge/public void, it fails program fit for neighborhood living even though the mass is cleanly contained and not visibly self-colliding. A stronger correction would be to preserve the dominant split-wing gesture but open the access side with a courtyard/notch or ground spine so the void becomes public and the section reads as inhabitable rather than merely split.
